summary: Map Cline Desktop UX, the sidecar transport, the Hub protocol, CLI/TUI features, auth/settings and Android integration constraints to ground a native M3 mobile app

architecture.rationale: Decision (final, per the owner's 'decide it now'): the app is a native Hub client for everything the Hub serves, plus a thin Termux-side bridge over the RUN_COMMAND intent for lifecycle and for the handful of surfaces the Hub does not expose. In the feature matrix, available_via=hub means the Hub WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub, frames {kind:command|reply|stream.subscribe|stream.unsubscribe|event} per sdk/packages/shared/src/hub.ts:975-990); available_via=sidecar means the Termux-side bridge: a background RUN_COMMAND running the installed $PREFIX/bin/cline (`cline auth`, `cline config --json`, `cline history --json`, `cline hub start|status|stop|upgrade`, `cline doctor --json`) or the `cline dashboard` server's /browser WebSocket (apps/cline-hub, already in the Termux tarball: release/build-termux-release.sh:174,202 stages dist/cline-hub and @cline/cline-hub is bundled into index.js by apps/cli/bun.mts packages:'bundle'); available_via=files means a RUN_COMMAND `cat`/write of a ~/.cline file; none means no kernel path (Android-native or omitted). Why the Hub is the primary channel (all verified in code, not from the dossier alone): (1) the chat loop is complete over the Hub: session.create, run.start/session.send_input (server timeout null), run.abort, assistant.delta/reasoning.delta/tool.started|updated|finished/usage.updated/session.notice/run.completed|failed|aborted, durable replay via stream.subscribe.sinceSequence, pending prompts (queue/steer), session.list/get/messages/search/update/delete/restore/update_connection, settings.list/toggle, schedule.*, task.*, connector.*, ui.notify (hub-server-transport.ts:794-923). (2) Approvals need no ownership: handleSessionCreate wires requestToolApprovalHandler for every session (hub-server-transport.ts:814-826), approval.requested is published to the session's subscribers and re-issued on every subscribe, and handleApprovalRespond accepts any registered client (approval-handlers.ts; the dossier's 'creator only' claim is wrong — only capability.* requests are target-bound). (3) The daemon does the heavy lifting itself when the client contributes nothing: tools readFile/search/bash/webFetch/applyPatch/editor run in the daemon (extensions/tools/executors/index.ts:97-109; Android bash = $PREFIX/bin/bash, shared/src/parse/shell.ts:14), checkpoints are created daemon-side when sessionConfig.checkpoint.enabled=true (local-runtime-bootstrap.ts:546-556 createCheckpointHooks), auto-compaction is daemon-side (local-runtime-host.ts:683 createContextCompactionPrepareTurn), and rules/skills/workflows/plugins/hooks load daemon-side because DEFAULT_RUNTIME_CONFIG_EXTENSIONS is all five kinds when configExtensions is omitted and no userInstructionService is contributed (shared/src/session/runtime-config.ts:19,45-50; runtime-builder.ts:455-480). Only ask_question needs a client contribution (definitions.ts:971 requires executors.askQuestion) and the skills tool likewise (definitions.ts:964). (4) Upgrade auth is the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol entry `cline-hub-auth.<token>` or a loopback Origin header; no Authorization header is read on the upgrade (hub-websocket-server.ts:675-691) — OkHttp can send either. (5) Every first-party front end (CLI TUI, desktop sidecar, dashboard) is itself a Hub client, so the Hub protocol is the surface upstream must keep stable; coupling the app to it is the lowest maintenance burden against upstream churn. Why a bridge is still required: the Hub has no provider/model catalog, credential CRUD, OAuth sign-in, account, MCP CRUD, marketplace, file search or workspace browsing (catalog.list, cline.account.get_current, prompt_commands.*, mention_files.search, session.fork are declared but never dispatched; settings.get/patch answer not_implemented — hub-server-transport.ts:783-932), it cannot start itself, and its token lives only in Termux-private ~/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json (0600; `cline hub status` never prints it). Those needs are met by (a) RUN_COMMAND `cline auth --provider X --apikey K --modelid M` (non-interactive, writes providers.json, sets lastUsedProvider), `cline auth cline` (WorkOS device flow, browser via xdg-open/termux-open), `cline config <target> --json`, `cline history --json|export`, `cline hub *`, `termux-wake-lock`; and (b) the shipped `cline dashboard --no-open` server for the richer settings surfaces (desktopCommand list verified in apps/cline-hub/src/server/desktop-commands.ts: list_provider_catalog, list_provider_models, save_provider_settings, add_provider, run_provider_oauth_login, cline_account, get_global_settings, set_telemetry_opt_out, set_auto_update_enabled, list/start/stop_connector_channel, list_mcp_servers, set_mcp_server_disabled, upsert_mcp_server, delete_mcp_server, ensure_mcp_settings_file, open_mcp_settings_file, get_process_context, list_cli_sessions, list_discovered_sessions, search_sessions, read_session_hooks, list_user_instruction_configs, list_marketplace_installed_entries, install/uninstall_marketplace_entry, uninstall_local_primitive, toggle_disabled_plugin_tool, set_tool_disabled, set_plugin_disabled; plus loadModels/loadProviderCatalog/saveProviderSettings/runProviderOAuthLogin messages). The dashboard is started on demand (it is a second Bun process with its own ClineCore) and the design degrades to RUN_COMMAND-only if its Bun.serve WebSocket turns out not to work on bun-android-ffi (blocking unknown 3): providers = `cline auth`, models = a bundled static list per provider plus free-text model id, account = omitted. Tier 1 and the Tier 2 core (sessions/history/model switch) depend only on the Hub and RUN_COMMAND.
architecture.rejected_alternatives: sidecar-in-termux (run apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar inside Termux and speak its ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport): rejected. It is not a runtime — it is itself a Hub client (ClineCore backendMode 'hub' + a 'code-sidecar-observer' NodeHubClient), so it adds a third ~300 MB-class Bun process on top of the Hub for no execution benefit; it hard-requires Bun.serve WebSockets on bun-android-ffi (unverified; the CLI port only exercises Bun as a ws client), an entry.js shim beside its own bundle, `ws` kept external, and a core build id identical to the CLI tarball's or the two will retire each other's Hub on every launch (compareHubBuilds in hub/discovery/index.ts); it silently auto-rejects every tool approval unless the client sends an allow-listed Origin plus the per-launch approval_token that is only printed on stdout (so the app would have to inject CLINE_SIDECAR_APPROVAL_TOKEN itself); it would need a new release artifact in the port; and its 113-command, unversioned protocol in apps/examples is coupled to the desktop webview and changes with every desktop release, with a third of it desktop-only (zenity/osascript folder picker, editor launch, Tauri updater/tray, remote SSH helpers, cloud sandboxes, Composio). The Hub protocol is versioned (v1) and durable; the sidecar's is neither. hub-direct only: rejected because it cannot bootstrap — no way to start the daemon, read the token, configure a provider or API key, sign in to Cline, list models, browse a workspace directory, or manage MCP/marketplace — and because upstream's design explicitly leaves credential and catalog management to in-process @cline/core helpers (local-provider-service.ts, ProviderSettingsManager) rather than the Hub. The Origin-header token-less upgrade path is not used as the default either: it is an upstream convenience for browser clients that may tighten, it grants only daemon-workspace authority (schedule/task scope), and the token is obtainable in one RUN_COMMAND. Also rejected: loading the `cline dashboard` webview in an Android WebView as the whole app (not Material 3, not the desktop feature set, and the owner asked for a native Compose app), and driving `cline --acp` over stdio (RUN_COMMAND stdin is one-shot and results arrive only on exit).

feature_matrix.feature: Kernel liveness and version probe
feature_matrix.kernel_api: GET http://127.0.0.1:25463/health (no auth: ok, protocolVersion, buildId, coreVersion, draining, url); GET /version (adds pid, startedAt, capabilities)
feature_matrix.notes: Replaces the sidebar Hub HoverCard dot and the boot gate. /version pid+startedAt detect a daemon restart (token rotation).

feature_matrix.feature: Start/stop/upgrade the Hub daemon, read the auth token, keep Termux alive
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND background: $PREFIX/bin/cline hub start|status|stop|upgrade; cat /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json (authToken, hubId, pid, url, port); termux-wake-lock / termux-wake-unlock
feature_matrix.notes: Desktop does this through ensureDetachedHubServer in-process. Needs v3.0.68-termux.2+ on the phone (entry.js + external ws). hub start takes 8-15 s cold on the S25U; its last stdout line is the ws URL.

feature_matrix.feature: Register client and subscribe to the event stream with replay
feature_matrix.kernel_api: command client.register {clientId, clientType:'android', transport:'native', actorKind:'client', capabilities:[{name:'approval.respond'},{name:'tool_executor.askQuestion'}], metadata, workspaceContext{workspaceRoot,cwd}}; frame stream.subscribe {clientId, sessionId?, sinceSequence?}; events carry sequence (durable log hub-events-hub-production.db)
feature_matrix.notes: Pending approval.requested events are re-issued on every subscribe (dedupe by approvalId). Hub-wide events (ui.notify, settings.changed, schedule.*, hub.client.*) only reach the global subscription.

feature_matrix.feature: New session (workspace, provider, model, mode, tool policy)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.create {workspaceRoot, cwd, sessionConfig:{providerId, modelId, mode:'act'|'plan', enableTools:true, enableSpawnAgent, enableAgentTeams, checkpoint:{enabled:true}, thinking?, reasoningEffort?, systemPrompt?}, metadata:{source:'android', interactive:true, title?, provider, model}, toolPolicies:{'*':{autoApprove:false|true}}} -> {session, snapshot}; event session.created
feature_matrix.notes: OMIT sessionConfig.apiKey so the daemon merges the stored key / refreshes OAuth (apiKey:'' wipes a stored plain key). Do not pass configExtensions: the default loads rules/skills/workflows/plugins/hooks daemon-side. metadata.source other than cli/vscode gives all built-in tools (incl. tasks).

feature_matrix.feature: Send prompt and stream the reply
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.send_input (= run.start) {prompt, mode?, delivery?, attachments?:{userImages:[dataURL...]}} with envelope.sessionId and timeoutMs:null; events run.started, assistant.delta{text}, assistant.finished{text}, iteration.started/finished, run.heartbeat (30 s), run.completed|failed|aborted {reason, error?, result{text,usage,finishReason}, snapshot}
feature_matrix.notes: The reply blocks for the whole turn; treat the run.* terminal event as truth so a dropped socket is recovered by replay.

feature_matrix.feature: Reasoning (thinking) blocks
feature_matrix.kernel_api: events reasoning.delta {text, redacted}, reasoning.finished {reasoning}
feature_matrix.notes: 'Thinking' / 'Thought for Ns' labels as in @cline/ui formatThoughtLabel.

feature_matrix.feature: Tool call rows (commands, edits, reads, web, MCP) with live output
feature_matrix.kernel_api: events tool.started {toolCallId, toolName, input}, tool.updated {toolCallId, toolName, update}, tool.finished {toolCallId, toolName, output, error?}; a second hook-derived tool.started/finished {toolName} without ids must be ignored
feature_matrix.notes: Same data the desktop renders via chat_tool_call_* chunks. Icons/summaries per TOOL_KIND_ICONS and tool-summary.ts.

feature_matrix.feature: Tool approval (approve / reject)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: event approval.requested {approvalId, sessionId, toolCallId, toolName, inputJson, iteration, agentId, conversationId, policy}; command approval.respond {approvalId, approved, reason?} -> {approvalId, approved}; event approval.resolved; session only prompts when toolPolicies autoApprove===false
feature_matrix.notes: No ownership check (approval-handlers.ts handleApprovalRespond). Rejection reason convention: 'This tool call was rejected by the user and not executed.' An unanswered approval parks the turn forever; always offer abort.

feature_matrix.feature: Stop / abort the agent
feature_matrix.kernel_api: run.abort {sessionId, reason?} -> {applied:true}; events run.aborted, approval.resolved{cancelled:true}
feature_matrix.notes: Also cancels pending approvals and capability requests.

feature_matrix.feature: Session status, notices and error banners
feature_matrix.kernel_api: events session.updated {session|snapshot} (status idle|running|pending|completed|aborted|failed), session.notice {message, noticeType recovery|stop|status, reason api_error|mistake_limit|auto_compaction|...}, run.failed {error}
feature_matrix.notes: Credential failures arrive as run.failed/session.notice api_error; map to the desktop's 'Sign in to Cline' / 'Open API providers' actions.

feature_matrix.feature: Token usage ring and cost
feature_matrix.kernel_api: event usage.updated {delta{inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens,totalCost}, totals, aggregateUsage}; session.get {includeSnapshot:true} usage/aggregateUsage; contextWindow from the model catalog
feature_matrix.notes: Context window size comes from list_provider_models (dashboard) or a bundled table; hide the ring when unknown, as the desktop does.

feature_matrix.feature: Android notifications (task completed, approval needed, question asked, session error)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: events ui.notify {title, body, severity, sessionId} (published by the Hub on completion), approval.requested, capability.requested (ask_question), run.failed
feature_matrix.notes: Needs the socket alive while backgrounded (foreground service) or is delivered on resume. Desktop's show_session_notification is Tauri-only.

feature_matrix.feature: Hub health indicator and transport states
feature_matrix.kernel_api: /health poll + WebSocket state; hub.status {} -> {hubId, draining, activeRpcTurns, pendingRuns, eventLog{lastSequence}, idle}; event hub.drain_changed
feature_matrix.notes: connecting | reconnecting | connected | unavailable as in desktop-client.ts, plus 'Termux asleep' when /health fails.

feature_matrix.feature: Provider setup minimal (API key + model id) for first run
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND: cline auth --provider <id> --apikey <key> --modelid <model> [--baseurl <url>] (exit 0, 'Provider configured: <id> (<model>)'); writes ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json and lastUsedProvider
feature_matrix.notes: Keeps keys in Termux so the TUI and the Hub share them; the app never stores provider secrets. Provider ids come from a bundled list (anthropic, openai-native, openrouter, gemini, xai, groq, mistral, deepseek, ollama, openai-compatible, ...).

feature_matrix.feature: Image attachments in prompts
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.send_input attachments.userImages: string[] of data: URLs (CLI pushes image.dataUrl, apps/cli/src/runtime/prompt.ts:194); userFiles are Termux filesystem paths
feature_matrix.notes: Photo picker -> downscale -> data URL. File attachments would need a RUN_COMMAND copy into Termux; defer.

feature_matrix.feature: Ask-question card (lettered options + free text)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.create runtimeOptions.clientContributions:[{kind:'toolExecutor', executor:'askQuestion', capabilityName:'tool_executor.askQuestion'}]; event capability.requested {requestId, targetClientId, capabilityName, payload{executor,args,context}}; command capability.respond {requestId, ok, payload:{result}} with envelope.clientId = targetClientId
feature_matrix.notes: Without the contribution the ask_question tool is simply absent (definitions.ts:971). The contribution is cancelled when the app disconnects, so hold the foreground service while a turn runs.

feature_matrix.feature: Queue / steer follow-ups and the prompt queue editor
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.send_input {delivery:'queue'|'steer'}; session.pending_prompts {sessionId} -> {prompts[{id,prompt,delivery,attachmentCount}]}; session.steer_first_pending_prompt; session.update_pending_prompt {promptId, prompt?, delivery?}; session.remove_pending_prompt {promptId}; events session.pending_prompts, session.pending_prompt_submitted
feature_matrix.notes: Composer placeholder 'Agent is working... submit to queue another message' when status is running.

feature_matrix.feature: Session list (sidebar, Pinned/Scheduled/Tasks, projects grouping)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.list {limit, rootOnly:true} -> {sessions: SessionRecord[]} (status, workspaceRoot, metadata{title, pinned, provider, model, prompt, source, scheduleId, totalCost, usage}, createdAt/updatedAt)
feature_matrix.notes: Persisted sessions from sessions.db, not only live ones. Poll on resume + session.created/updated events; no 12 s poller.

feature_matrix.feature: Session search
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.search {query, limit<=200, workspaceRoot?} -> {hits[{sessionId, documentId, role, title, snippet, startedAt, workspaceRoot, score}]}
feature_matrix.notes: FTS5 index; may be empty when unavailable.

feature_matrix.feature: Open / resume a history session
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.messages {sessionId} -> {messages: MessageWithMetadata[]} (works for non-live sessions: readHubSessionRecord + readSessionMessages); live: session.attach {sessionId}; not live after a daemon restart: session.create {sessionConfig:{sessionId:<old>, providerId, modelId,...}, initialMessages:<messages>, metadata} (isReadOnlyResumeStart, local-runtime-host.ts:409-414)
feature_matrix.notes: Transcript rows: role user|assistant with content blocks text/image/tool_use/tool_result/thinking; render tool_use+tool_result pairs as tool rows like read_session_messages does.

feature_matrix.feature: Rename, pin, session metadata
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.update {sessionId, title?, metadata?:{pinned?}} -> {updated, session}; event session.updated
feature_matrix.notes: Server strips autoApproveTools and hubCapabilityOwnerClientId from client metadata.

feature_matrix.feature: Delete session
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.delete {sessionId, deleteCheckpointRefs?} -> {deleted}
feature_matrix.notes: Task-worktree removal is sidecar-only; not applicable.

feature_matrix.feature: Fork session
feature_matrix.kernel_api: client-side: session.messages -> session.create {initialMessages, metadata:{fork:{forkedFromSessionId, forkedAt, source}}} (session.fork is declared in HubCommandName but never dispatched)
feature_matrix.notes: Same approach as the CLI's forkCurrentSession.

feature_matrix.feature: Model / provider switch mid-session
feature_matrix.kernel_api: session.update_connection {sessionId, updates:{providerId?, modelId?, thinking?, reasoningEffort?, thinkingBudgetTokens?, apiKey?, baseUrl?}} -> {sessionId, updated:true}
feature_matrix.notes: Stored credentials for the new provider are merged daemon-side; omit apiKey.

feature_matrix.feature: Reasoning effort selector (None/Low/Medium/High/Extra)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: sessionConfig.thinking/reasoningEffort at create; session.update_connection thinking:false|null clears; values low|medium|high|xhigh
feature_matrix.notes: Disabled when the model lacks reasoning (ProviderModel.supportsReasoning from the catalog).

feature_matrix.feature: Plan / Act mode
feature_matrix.kernel_api: sessionConfig.mode at create; per-turn session.send_input {mode:'act'|'plan'|'yolo'}
feature_matrix.notes: Desktop hides the toggle (className hidden) but the CLI exposes it; ship it as the CLI does.

feature_matrix.feature: Auto-approve all toggle
feature_matrix.kernel_api: toolPolicies at session.create only (session.update strips autoApproveTools); flipping = recreate the session with sessionConfig.sessionId + initialMessages (what the CLI's restartWithCurrentMessages does)
feature_matrix.notes: Persist the app default locally; the CLI's own persisted default lives in global-settings.json toolAutoApprove.

feature_matrix.feature: Provider catalog (configured / popular / all, auth kind, config fields)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard ws://127.0.0.1:8787/browser desktopCommand list_provider_catalog -> {providers: ProviderListItem[], settingsPath}; fallback RUN_COMMAND cat providers.json (configured ids only)
feature_matrix.notes: ProviderListItem carries the plaintext apiKey; keep it in memory only, loopback only. Dashboard started on demand: RUN_COMMAND cline dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787.

feature_matrix.feature: Model list per provider (featured Recommended/Free tiers, capabilities)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard {type:'loadModels', providerId} -> {type:'models', providerId, models} or desktopCommand list_provider_models {provider}
feature_matrix.notes: No Hub or CLI JSON command lists models. Fallback: bundled static lists (FALLBACK_PROVIDER_MODELS) plus free-text model id.

feature_matrix.feature: Save provider settings (key, base URL, enable/disable), add OpenAI-compatible provider
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard desktopCommand save_provider_settings {provider, enabled?, api_key?, base_url?}, add_provider {provider_id, name, base_url, api_key?, models, default_model_id}; fallback RUN_COMMAND cline auth --provider --apikey --modelid --baseurl
feature_matrix.notes: enabled:false deletes the entry and clears legacy secrets.json keys (sign-out).

feature_matrix.feature: Sign in with Cline (device-code OAuth) and sign out
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND cline auth cline (WorkOS device flow; opens verification_uri_complete via xdg-open->termux-open; exits when tokens are saved) or dashboard runProviderOAuthLogin {providerId:'cline'} -> provider_oauth_login_done; sign-out = save_provider_settings {provider:'cline', enabled:false}
feature_matrix.notes: The device code is prefilled in the URL, so the app needs no code display if the browser opens; if xdg-open is missing under the background shell, run the command with the foreground (terminal) runner so the user sees URL+code in Termux.

feature_matrix.feature: Welcome setup notice (no provider connected)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND cat ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json -> lastUsedProvider + providers map (or dashboard list_provider_catalog configured flags)
feature_matrix.notes: Read once at launch and after any auth action; never persist the file contents.

feature_matrix.feature: Workspace picker (choose a folder for a new session)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/find <dir> -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d (stdout list) + typed path; validity confirmed by session.create (list_workspace_directories/pick_workspace_directory are sidecar-only)
feature_matrix.notes: Default roots: $HOME and ~/storage/shared if termux-setup-storage was run. Remember recent workspaces locally.

feature_matrix.feature: Kernel settings: wake lock, keep Hub running, stop kernel, hub upgrade
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND termux-wake-lock|termux-wake-unlock, cline hub stop, cline hub upgrade --wait 30; /version buildId vs installed
feature_matrix.notes: Desktop equivalent is the Hub update dialog + hub_upgrade. Upstream's Hub has no idle exit (~300 MB RSS on the S25U), so expose an explicit stop.

feature_matrix.feature: Diff view (uncommitted changes per session, per-file hunks, +/- counts)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: derived from tool.finished payloads of editor/apply_patch/write tools (input + output), same as desktop lib/session-diff.ts over chat_tool_call_* chunks; history via session.messages tool_use/tool_result blocks
feature_matrix.notes: No generic file read/diff command exists on the Hub or the sidecar; the desktop derives diffs from tool payloads too.

feature_matrix.feature: Terminal / command output with ANSI
feature_matrix.kernel_api: tool.started {input{command}}, tool.updated {update} streaming chunks, tool.finished {output, error}
feature_matrix.notes: Needs an ANSI-to-AnnotatedString renderer; exact update chunk shape for run_commands to be read in executors/bash.ts before building it.

feature_matrix.feature: Proceed while a command keeps running
feature_matrix.kernel_api: run.proceed_while_running {sessionId, toolCallId?} -> {detachedCount}
feature_matrix.notes: Show the button on long-running command rows as the desktop does for toolDetachable.

feature_matrix.feature: Checkpoints: edit-and-restart from a message, revert workspace
feature_matrix.kernel_api: checkpoint history from session.get {includeSnapshot:true} snapshot.checkpoint.history / message metadata; session.restore {sessionId, checkpointRunCount, restore:{messages:true, workspace:true|false}, sessionConfig, metadata} -> {session, snapshot, messages, checkpoint}; checkpoints are created daemon-side when sessionConfig.checkpoint.enabled=true
feature_matrix.notes: Desktop dialogs 'Revert to this checkpoint?' and 'Edit and restart from here?' map to restore with/without a new prompt.

feature_matrix.feature: @file mentions / workspace file search
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND rg --files <workspace> | head -2000 (or find -type f) cached in the app; mention_files.search is undispatched on the Hub
feature_matrix.notes: Attach as userFiles paths (Termux paths) so the daemon reads them.

feature_matrix.feature: Slash commands for skills and workflows
feature_matrix.kernel_api: list: settings.list {workspaceRoot, cwd} snapshot.skills/workflows (id, name, path, enabled); invoke: the daemon's own user-instruction service handles skills when the skills executor exists, otherwise inline the file: RUN_COMMAND cat <item.path> and send as a user_command block like expandUserCommandPrompt
feature_matrix.notes: createDefaultExecutors has no skills executor (definitions.ts:964 gates the skills tool); verify whether the daemon registers one for Hub sessions before relying on /skill passthrough.

feature_matrix.feature: Git branch display, branch list/checkout, worktree
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND git -C <ws> branch --show-current / for-each-ref / checkout; create_git_worktree is sidecar-only
feature_matrix.notes: Branch label in the header; checkout and worktree are tier 4.

feature_matrix.feature: Customize: rules / skills / workflows / plugins / tools / MCP toggles
feature_matrix.kernel_api: settings.list {cwd, workspaceRoot, includePluginTools:true} -> {snapshot{workflows,rules,plugins,skills,tools,mcp}}; settings.toggle {type: skills|plugins|tools|mcp, id|path|name, enabled?} -> {snapshot, changedTypes}; event settings.changed
feature_matrix.notes: Rules/workflows are not toggleable (same as desktop). Hooks list via RUN_COMMAND cline config hooks --json.

feature_matrix.feature: MCP server list / add / edit / delete / OAuth
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard desktopCommand list_mcp_servers, upsert_mcp_server, delete_mcp_server, set_mcp_server_disabled, ensure_mcp_settings_file; OAuth via RUN_COMMAND cline mcp (wizard, foreground runner)
feature_matrix.notes: authorize_mcp_server_oauth is desktop-sidecar-only.

feature_matrix.feature: Marketplace browse / install / uninstall (skills, MCP, plugins)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard GET /api/marketplace/catalog; desktopCommand list_marketplace_installed_entries, install_marketplace_entry, uninstall_marketplace_entry, uninstall_local_primitive
feature_matrix.notes: Installs run git clones inside Termux.

feature_matrix.feature: Schedules (routines): list, create, edit, pause/resume, run now, runs history
feature_matrix.kernel_api: schedule.list/get/create/update/delete/enable/disable/trigger/list_executions/stats/active/upcoming; events schedule.*; requires a registered client with workspaceContext.workspaceRoot; allWorkspaces needs token auth
feature_matrix.notes: Scheduled sessions run inside the daemon; they need Termux alive at fire time (wake lock).

feature_matrix.feature: Account (credits balance, usage, billing, organizations, switch)
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard desktopCommand cline_account {operation: fetchMe|fetchBalance|fetchUserOrganizations|fetchOrganizationBalance|fetchUsageTransactions|fetchPaymentTransactions|switchAccount}
feature_matrix.notes: Returns {signedIn:false, code:'ACCOUNT_NOT_AUTHENTICATED'} when signed out.

feature_matrix.feature: Global settings: telemetry opt-out, auto-update
feature_matrix.kernel_api: dashboard desktopCommand get_global_settings, set_telemetry_opt_out {telemetry_opt_out}, set_auto_update_enabled {auto_update_enabled} (file ~/.cline/data/settings/global-settings.json)
feature_matrix.notes: Auto-update is irrelevant on the Termux port (installer-managed); show telemetry only.

feature_matrix.feature: Agents roster (subagents / teams) and team progress
feature_matrix.kernel_api: event team.progress; session.list {rootOnly:false} children via metadata.parentSessionId; events carry payload.agent {kind lead|subagent|teammate}
feature_matrix.notes: assistant.delta has no agent field; follow the CLI's use-agent-events.ts handling.

feature_matrix.feature: Session export (HTML / JSON) and share
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND cline history export <id> -o ~/storage/downloads/<id>.html then Android share of the file (needs termux-setup-storage)
feature_matrix.notes: CLI-only feature; cheap to add.

feature_matrix.feature: Diagnostics export
feature_matrix.kernel_api: RUN_COMMAND cline doctor --json; tail of ~/.cline/data/logs/hub-daemon.log and cline.log (100 KB result cap)

synthesis.pairing_and_lifecycle:
PREREQUISITES ON THE PHONE: Termux >= 0.109 (S25U has 0.118.x), allow-external-apps=true in ~/.termux/termux.properties (the owner confirmed it is already set), Cline Termux port >= v3.0.68-termux.2 (first build whose Hub daemon starts: entry.js + external ws; the current stable .1 cannot start it), optionally termux-setup-storage for workspace folders under ~/storage. Nothing else is installed in Termux by the app.

APP MANIFEST: android.permission.INTERNET; com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND (custom dangerous permission -> declare and request at runtime; the grant dialog is Termux's); <queries><package android:name="com.termux"/></queries> (API 30+ visibility); POST_NOTIFICATIONS (API 33+); FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE with <property android:name="android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE" android:value="hub-session"/> (no timeout; sideloaded app), optionally FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC as the Play-clean alternative with the 6 h/24 h budget; res/xml/network_security_config.xml with <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"><domain>127.0.0.1</domain></domain-config> because ws:// to loopback is cleartext on API 28-36; an exported="false" BroadcastReceiver for RUN_COMMAND results.

RUN_COMMAND BRIDGE (one Kotlin class, every call typed): Intent action com.termux.RUN_COMMAND, component com.termux/com.termux.app.RunCommandService, started with startService() from a foreground state. Extras: com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_PATH = absolute executable (/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/cline | cat | find | termux-wake-lock | termux-wake-unlock | pkill), com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_ARGUMENTS = String[] (no ~ expansion in arguments: use /data/data/com.termux/files/home/...), com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_WORKDIR = /data/data/com.termux/files/home, com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_BACKGROUND = true (APP_SHELL runner; no terminal session, no activity), com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_PENDING_INTENT = PendingIntent.getBroadcast(FLAG_MUTABLE or FLAG_ONE_SHOT) targeting the app's own receiver. Result Bundle extra "result": stdout, stderr, exitCode, err (-1 = none), errmsg; stdout+stderr truncated to 100 KB combined, so never use it for logs or transcripts. Results arrive only when the command exits; long-running commands (dashboard) are fire-and-poll. For the Cline OAuth sign-in where the browser cannot be opened from the background shell, use the foreground runner (BACKGROUND=false, SESSION_ACTION=0) so the user sees URL and code in Termux.

CONNECT SEQUENCE (every app start and every resume): 1) GET http://127.0.0.1:25463/health with a 1 s timeout; if ok, require protocolVersion "v1" and remember buildId/coreVersion; GET /version gives pid+startedAt. 2) If refused: RUN_COMMAND `cline hub start` (background; exits when the daemon is up, last stdout line = ws URL; 8-15 s cold on the S25U), then RUN_COMMAND `termux-wake-lock` (acquires Termux's PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK + WifiLock and keeps TermuxService in foreground-service state, which is what keeps the Hub alive: the Hub is a detached child in Termux's process group and dies with it). 3) Token: if the cached token's (hubId, pid, startedAt) differ from /version, RUN_COMMAND `cat /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json` and parse {authToken (64 hex), hubId, pid, port, url, buildId, coreVersion}; store authToken in DataStore encrypted with an Android Keystore AES key (never log it; never write it to the repo). The token rotates on every daemon start. 4) OkHttp WebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub with request header Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: cline-hub-auth.<token>; on HTTP 401 re-read the token once; keep the no-token path (Origin: http://localhost, reduced authority) only as a diagnostic fallback behind a developer switch. 5) Send command {version:"v1", command:"client.register", requestId, clientId, payload:{clientId, clientType:"android", displayName:"Cline for Android", transport:"native", actorKind:"client", capabilities:[{name:"approval.respond"},{name:"tool_executor.askQuestion"}], metadata:{version, platform:"android", pid:0}, workspaceContext:{workspaceRoot:<last workspace>, cwd:<same>}, protocolVersion:"v1"}}; clientId is a stable per-install id ("android-<uuid>") reused across reconnects like NodeHubClient. 6) Frame {kind:"stream.subscribe", clientId, sinceSequence:<persisted global cursor>} and, for each open session, {kind:"stream.subscribe", clientId, sessionId, sinceSequence:<persisted per-session cursor>}; persist the highest sequence seen per key after every event; pending approvals are re-issued on each subscribe (dedupe by approvalId). 7) For an open session that is live: session.attach {sessionId}; for one that is not (daemon restarted): session.create {sessionConfig:{sessionId:<old>,...}, initialMessages:<session.messages result>}.

KEEP-ALIVE: the Hub pings every 30 s and terminates a socket that misses one sweep; OkHttp pongs automatically while the process is unfrozen. Android freezes a cached app ~10 s after it leaves the foreground and kills its TCP sockets, so: start the specialUse foreground service (notification "Cline is working...") when a turn starts or a session is attached with "keep connected" on, stop it when the run ends (run.completed|failed|aborted) and no approval/question is pending; otherwise accept the disconnect and resync on resume. All command replies must be optional: terminal truth is the event stream, and session.send_input is issued with timeoutMs:null and the request kept only as a correlation id. Reconnect policy copied from NodeHubClient: delay min(250 ms * 2^attempt, 5 s) with 50 % jitter, re-register with the same clientId, re-subscribe with cursors, re-attach sessions; pending commands fail with hub_connection_closed and are not retried except idempotent reads.

TERMUX LIVENESS AND THE HUB'S LIFETIME: the Hub has no idle exit (~300 MB RSS measured on the S25U) and dies when TermuxService stops and Termux is evicted (AOSP kills the whole process group). The app therefore: holds termux-wake-lock while "connected", offers "Stop kernel" (RUN_COMMAND `cline hub stop`, then `termux-wake-unlock`) and "Disconnect (keep Hub)" in Kernel settings, shows a "Termux asleep / Hub down" state when /health fails and offers "Start kernel", and shows the One UI checklist once (Termux and this app: Battery > Unrestricted; add both to Never sleeping apps; Developer options > Disable child process restrictions, verifiable with adb `settings get global settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs`). Before shipping, the owner's pending decision in CLAUDE.local.md (is a Hub left running in the background acceptable?) becomes the default of the "keep Hub running after exit" switch.

ON-DEMAND SETTINGS HELPER (the shipped dashboard server): when the user opens Providers, Account, MCP or Marketplace: GET http://127.0.0.1:8787/health; if down, RUN_COMMAND background `cline dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787` (the command does not exit; poll /health up to 20 s), then OkHttp WebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:8787/browser with header Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8787 (both Host and Origin must be in the allow-list; no roomSecret on loopback); send {type:"ready"}, then {type:"desktopCommand", id, command, args} -> {type:"desktopCommandResult", id, ok, result|error}, {type:"loadModels", providerId} -> {type:"models"}, {type:"loadProviderCatalog"} -> {type:"provider_catalog"}, {type:"runProviderOAuthLogin", providerId} -> {type:"provider_oauth_login_done"}. The dashboard also ensures the Hub and registers as "cline-hub-chat"/"cline-hub-server" clients. Stop it when leaving settings: RUN_COMMAND `pkill -f "index.js dashboard"`. If blocking unknown 3 fails (Bun.serve on the device Bun), this helper is dropped and the same screens fall back to RUN_COMMAND `cline auth ...` plus bundled model lists.

RECOVERY MATRIX: upgrade 401 -> stale token -> re-read production.json; ECONNREFUSED on 25463 -> `cline hub start`; RUN_COMMAND result err != -1 with errmsg mentioning allow-external-apps or permission -> Kernel setup screen with the exact fix; Termux not resolvable via <queries> -> "Install Termux" screen; reply error hub_draining (retryable) -> wait for hub.drain_changed; session_not_found on send -> resume via session.create with sessionConfig.sessionId + initialMessages; run.interrupted {reason:"hub_restart"} -> mark the run interrupted and offer resend; approval.requested with no UI able to answer (app killed) -> re-issued on next subscribe, plus the notification deep-links to the session; capability.requested (ask_question) after reconnect -> cancelled by the Hub when the target client unregisters, so the turn continues without the answer; a RUN_COMMAND that never returns (hub start hung) -> 60 s timeout then `cline doctor --json` for diagnostics.

blocking_unknowns: 1. Hub WebSocket subprotocol echo on the device: the Hub server runs under the device Bun's built-in `ws` replacement (the port keeps `ws` external), and OkHttp fails a handshake whose 101 does not echo `cline-hub-auth.<token>`. The CLI's own client (also Bun's native WebSocket) connects, which suggests the echo works, but it is unproven for OkHttp. Experiment (5 min, S25U via adb/ssh, outside release windows): `cline hub start`, then an OkHttp or `curl -i -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: cline-hub-auth.<token>' --http1.1 -H 'Upgrade: websocket' -H 'Connection: Upgrade' -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==' -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13' http://127.0.0.1:25463/hub` and check the response header. Fallback if it fails: Origin: http://localhost without a subprotocol (reduced authority).

2. The Hub only starts from v3.0.68-termux.2 (commits a350d0d74 entry.js, 54388558c external ws, 1ebf0a433) which is committed locally, unpushed and unreleased; the installed stable .1 cannot run the Hub at all. The app's Tier 1 cannot be tested on the phone until that candidate is installed on the S25U (plan item 2: push, `manage.sh candidate cli-v3.0.68 --revision 2`, manual test). Not a code unknown, but the first gate.

3. Bun.serve WebSocket upgrades on bun-android-ffi 1.4.0-canary.1 are unverified; this decides whether the shipped `cline dashboard` server can be the settings helper. Experiment: on the S25U run `cline dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787`, `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8787/health`, then a WebSocket handshake to /browser with `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8787`. If it fails, Providers/Account/MCP/Marketplace use the RUN_COMMAND-only fallback (`cline auth`, bundled model lists, no account tab).

4. Background RUN_COMMAND environment for the launcher: $PREFIX/bin/cline execs `node cline-node-wrapper.cjs` when ca-certs.cjs is present (install-cline-termux.sh:478-519), so `node` must be on the APP_SHELL PATH, LD_PRELOAD (termux-exec) and HOME must be set as in a login shell, and `cline hub start` must detach correctly from a RunCommandService task. Experiment via adb (the owner allowed adb): `adb shell am startservice --user 0 -n com.termux/com.termux.app.RunCommandService -a com.termux.RUN_COMMAND --es com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_PATH /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/cline --esa com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_ARGUMENTS hub,status --ez com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_BACKGROUND true`, then check ~/.cline/data/logs for the result (or run the app's own spike with the PendingIntent receiver).

5. Browser opening from the kernel on Android for OAuth flows: `cline auth cline` (apps/cli/src/utils/open.ts -> the `open` package) and the dashboard's openExternalUrl (spawns xdg-open) both depend on termux-tools' xdg-open/termux-open working from a background shell. Experiment: RUN_COMMAND `xdg-open https://example.com` in background mode. If it fails, run the sign-in command with the foreground (terminal) runner so the user sees URL and code in Termux; the WorkOS verification_uri_complete carries the code.

6. End-to-end resume of a persisted session after a daemon restart over the Hub: session.create with sessionConfig.sessionId=<old> + initialMessages=<session.messages result> takes the isReadOnlyResumeStart path (local-runtime-host.ts:409-414 verified), but whether usage, checkpoint history and compaction state come back, and whether run.start then continues the conversation correctly, was not traced. Experiment on the workstation (no device): `cline hub start`, create a session with the CLI, `cline hub stop && cline hub start`, replay the sequence with a scripted ws client against Bun 1.4.2.

7. Per-tool approval policy keys: toolPolicies['*'] is enough for the auto-approve toggle, but per-tool rules (desktop 'Off = safe tools auto-approved, others prompt') need the headless tool names resolveToolPolicy matches (read_files? run_commands? editor?) — read sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts:2417-2432 resolveToolPolicy and sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts tool names before implementing the per-tool matrix.

8. Streaming shape of tool.updated for run_commands (incremental stdout chunks vs cumulative, ANSI preserved?) and for editor/apply_patch (diff hunks in output?) — read sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts and the editor/apply_patch executors plus sdk/packages/shared/src/agents/types.ts before building the terminal and diff renderers (Tier 3).

9. Whether the daemon registers a `skills` executor for Hub-hosted sessions (createDefaultExecutors has none; definitions.ts:964 gates the skills tool on executors.skills) and therefore whether /skill prompts pass through or must be inlined by the app from the skill file (RUN_COMMAND cat). Read sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-client-contributions.ts createDefaultToolExecutors paths and local-runtime-host session build.

10. Re-registration with the same clientId from a new connection while the Hub still holds the stale registration (half-open socket before the 30-60 s heartbeat sweep): client-handlers.ts handleClientRegister was not read to the end; NodeHubClient reuses its clientId, which suggests replacement is tolerated. Read handleClientRegister or, if rejected (client_already_registered), mint a fresh clientId per connection and re-attach sessions.

11. Phantom-process and battery state on the S25U (settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs, Termux battery exemption, Developer options 'Disable child process restrictions'): checkable now with `adb shell settings get global settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs` and `adb shell dumpsys deviceidle whitelist | grep termux`; affects reliability of long tool runs, not the design.

12. Owner decision still open from CLAUDE.local.md plan item 2: whether a Hub left running in the background (no idle exit, ~300 MB RSS) is acceptable; it sets the default of the app's 'keep kernel running after exit' switch and whether the app should auto-stop the Hub when the last session ends.

13. readers.summary: Read-only inventory of Cline Desktop's webview (apps/examples/desktop-app/webview, Next.js app router, single page app/page.tsx with reducer-based back/forward navigation instead of URL routes) and the shared @cline/ui package it imports (sdk/packages/ui: agent-chat primitives, composer, session row, approval/question cards, PR bar, changes panel, Radix-derived OKLCH/hex token theme). Top-level views: chat (welcome state or conversation), sessions table, settings overlay with sections General | Providers | Voice | Channels(hidden) | Schedules | Import | Remote | Account | About plus Customize (installed hub) and Marketplace (explorer), onboarding overlay (welcome/connect/github/import/done), and a cloud-provisioning pane. The webview talks to a Bun sidecar over ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport with 113 named commands (incl. chat_session_command with actions start/send/attach/abort/reset/fork/restore_checkpoint/steer_prompt/pending_prompts/update_pending_prompt/remove_pending_prompt and proceed_while_running) and 21 push events (chat_event streams chat_text/chat_reasoning/chat_tool_call_start/chat_tool_call_update/chat_usage/chat_media/chat_queued_prompt_start/chat_done/chat_core_log/stdout/stderr). Eleven commands are Tauri-native only (notifications, tray, updater, app icon, folder picker, quit/relaunch). Every item below gives files and the user-visible behaviour; copy strings are quoted verbatim where they matter for parity.
risks: The desktop webview never speaks to the Hub directly: every command above goes to the Bun sidecar (ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport) which wraps @cline/core. An Android front end that targets the Termux Hub (ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub) must either port the sidecar's 113-command surface or map each screen onto Hub RPCs; this inventory lists the webview-side names only, not the Hub protocol.

Eleven commands and several surfaces are Tauri-native only (desktop notifications, tray status, auto-updater/App update indicator, app icon picker, folder picker, Windows title-bar controls, quit/relaunch, window-focus suppression). They need Android equivalents or omission.

Several surfaces are hidden or gated in this build: Channels (HIDDEN_SECTIONS), Plan/Act toggle (className hidden), Agenda/Todo UI (AGENDA_UI_ENABLED=false), Cloud sessions ('Coming soon' unless cloudAgentsAvailable/feature flag), GitHub onboarding step (feature flag code-onboarding-github), Composio connectors (org beta). Reproducing them faithfully may expose features upstream does not consider shipped.
Rich-text rendering depends on Streamdown + shiki code highlighting + ANSI parsing + per-hunk diff rendering; a Compose app needs its own Markdown/diff/ANSI renderers to match the transcript.

Interaction model is pointer-first: HoverCards (session overview, hub status), right-click ContextMenus (pin/rename/fork/delete), hover-revealed row actions, keyboard chords (Cmd/Ctrl+N/P/,). Only one surface has a touch breakpoint (model picker <=560 px); the sidebar/settings layouts assume desktop widths.

Marketplace catalog is fetched through a Next.js API route (/api/marketplace/catalog) proxied by the sidecar, and release notes through /api/changelog; neither exists on the phone without the sidecar.
OAuth sign-in relies on a browser round trip with a device code pushed by provider_oauth_user_code and a 15-minute client timeout; Account/Providers/Onboarding all assume this flow.

Many list views keep module-level caches with TTLs (extension inventory 60 s, hook stats 30 s, routine overview 30 s, history poll 12 s, PR status 30 s, update status 30 s); matching perceived freshness on a phone affects battery and the Termux phantom-process budget.
unknowns: hooks/use-chat-session.ts (4281 lines) was read only in part: the exact reducer that turns chat_event streams and chat_session_command responses into messages/checkpoints/fileDiffs, and the activityLabel sources beyond the imported-history summary, were not traced line by line.
The sidecar handler registry was not read, so commands the sidecar supports but the webview never calls (if any) are not listed, and argument/response schemas were inferred from call sites only.

lib/cloud-repositories.ts, lib/composio-types.ts, lib/streaming-transcription.ts, lib/session-diff.ts, lib/workspace-paths.ts, hooks/use-agenda-tasks.ts, hooks/use-session-agents.ts and @cline/ui agent-chat.css / tool-summary were not opened; their behaviour is described from how callers use them.
Exact visual specs (spacing, animation curves, hero artwork) live in agent-chat.css, agent-welcome-hero.css and the Storybook stories, which were not read.

A second working directory ~/workspace/cline-termux-app was added mid-task; it was not inspected (outside this read-only lens on the desktop app), so nothing here reflects what that project already contains.

readers.summary: The Cline Desktop "sidecar" (apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar, entry sidecar/index.ts) is a Bun process that serves ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport (plus HTTP /health, /shutdown, /telemetry/error, /api/marketplace/catalog) with a 3-frame JSON protocol: {type:"command",id,command,args} → {type:"response",id,ok,result?,error?} and server-push {type:"event",event:{name,payload}}. It is NOT an agent runtime: it embeds @cline/core's ClineCore in backendMode "hub" (HubRuntimeHost), so every session, run, approval and checkpoint is executed by the shared Hub daemon (ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub, token in ~/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json); the sidecar is a Hub client + observer that re-shapes Hub/Core events into ~22 webview event names (chat_event with ~11 stream kinds, chat_session_status/ended, tool_approval_state, ask_question_*, prompts_in_queue_state, …) and answers ~110 command names (chat_session_command with 12 actions, session discovery/CRUD, providers, voice, MCP, git/worktrees, routines, agenda tasks, plugins/marketplace, connectors, SSH remotes, account/cloud). Auth is a per-launch approval_token query param plus an Origin allow-list; a connection without a trusted Origin+token still works but can never receive or answer tool approvals (they are auto-rejected). Running it inside Termux is plausible but conditional: it hard-requires Bun (Bun.serve websocket; throws on Node), bun:sqlite, the `ws` package over node:http for the Hub client (must stay external on bun-android-ffi, same as the CLI fix 54388558c), an entry.js shim beside its bundle so it can spawn/become the Hub daemon, a matching core build id with the CLI bundle so the two do not retire each other's Hub, and an Android app that sends an Origin header from the allow-list plus the token (seeded via CLINE_SIDECAR_APPROVAL_TOKEN through RUN_COMMAND, since the token is otherwise only printed on the sidecar's stdout). Desktop-only commands (folder picker via zenity/kdialog/osascript, editor launch, Tauri updater/tray/notifications) have no Android counterpart and must be reimplemented natively.
risks: Bun.serve with the websocket handler on bun-android-ffi 1.4.0-canary.1 is unverified: the CLI port only exercises Bun as a client (fetch, ws) and bun:sqlite; a sidecar that cannot bind/upgrade on the device is dead on arrival. Test `BunRuntime.serve({websocket})` on the S25U before committing to the sidecar route.

Hub ownership conflict: a sidecar bundle whose embedded core build id/epoch differs from the CLI tarball's will retire the CLI-started Hub (and vice versa) on every launch, interrupting the other client's sessions; prompts are suppressed because coreVersion matches, so it would look like random Hub restarts. Build both from one core dist or pin CLINE_HUB_BUILD_ID/CLINE_HUB_BUILD_EPOCH_MS.

Approval dead-end: an Android client that omits Origin or the approval_token gets a working chat where every approval-requiring tool is auto-rejected (or, with the default autoApproveTools !== false, auto-approved) with no error surfaced on the socket.

The send action blocks for the entire agent turn (minutes); with Android Doze / Termux backgrounded, a dropped socket rejects the pending request and the sidecar's LiveSession busy state is only recovered via attach + chat_session_status, so the app needs the same reconnect + attach-on-hydrate logic as the webview (and a wake lock while a turn runs).

Session discovery has a destructive side effect: list_chat_sessions rm -rf's any <sessions>/<id> directory without a sessions.db row. Running a sidecar built from a different core schema/version than the CLI against the same ~/.cline could delete artifacts the CLI still expects.

Process budget: sidecar + Hub daemon + plugin sandbox + MCP servers + agent shells all count against Android's phantom-process limit (32) and Termux's foreground state; the existing 7 s PTY gate already shows the device deprioritising background Termux.

Memory and disk: a Bun sidecar bundle is another ~40 MB transpiler cache per release (the CLI already relocates its cache in-tree) and a second process holding sqlite handles on sessions.db/teams.db concurrently with the CLI/Hub.
unknowns: Whether bun-android-ffi's Bun.serve accepts WebSocket upgrades and delivers `message`/`close` callbacks reliably (not tested in this repo; no Android target in build-sidecar-bin.ts).

Whether `xdg-open` exists on the test devices (termux-tools normally provides it as a wrapper over termux-open) — the repo does not say; open_external_url would otherwise reject with 'could not open browser'.
What os.userInfo().shell returns under Termux/Bionic (affects only ensureLoginShellPath's fallback to /bin/bash; failure is non-fatal).

Whether the Hub WebSocket server accepts an `authToken` query parameter in addition to the `cline-hub-auth.<token>` subprotocol and Bearer header — the client strips ?authToken and moves it into the subprotocol; server-side query handling was not read.
Exact payload of the `read_session_hooks` and `list_session_agents` results beyond their TypeScript names (artifacts.ts / agents.ts were not read in full).

Whether the webview sends a real apiKey in ChatSessionConfig or an empty string that core resolves from providers.json — chat-schema requires a string, buildCoreSessionConfig forwards it; the resolution path inside the Hub runtime was not traced.
Exact CoreSessionEvent 'chunk' stream names other than the chat_* set (any non-'agent' stream is forwarded verbatim); not enumerated here.

readers.summary: Hub WebSocket protocol (cli-v3.0.68 + Termux port, read-only audit of sdk/packages/core/src/hub/{server,client,daemon,discovery,runtime-host} and sdk/packages/shared/src/hub.ts). Wire: ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub (CLINE_HUB_PORT=25463; dev 25466), JSON text frames `{kind: command|reply|stream.subscribe|stream.unsubscribe|event, ...}`, protocol "v1" (min=max=v1). Auth on the upgrade is the WebSocket subprotocol `cline-hub-auth.<token>` (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol), NOT an Authorization header; Bearer is only for the HTTP side routes (/status, /drain, /shutdown). A loopback client that sends an `Origin: http://localhost` header is accepted WITHOUT the token (origin-auth path), losing only cross-workspace registration rights. Token = 64-hex randomBytes(32), regenerated on every daemon start, published in ~/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json (production owner) together with url/pid/buildId; `cline hub status` prints url/pid/startedAt but not the token. Events are durable (SQLite hub-events-hub-production.db, 7 d/200k rows/64 MiB) and cursor-replayable via `stream.subscribe.sinceSequence`; pending tool approvals are re-issued to every new subscriber. Server pings every 30 s and terminates sockets that miss a pong by the next sweep; the reference client reconnects with 250 ms→5 s jittered backoff, re-registers under the same clientId and re-subscribes with its last sequence. VERDICT: a thin Android client CAN run a complete interactive chat purely over the Hub: session.create (with sessionConfig.providerId/modelId, metadata.source/interactive, toolPolicies {"*":{autoApprove:false}} to get approval prompts), run.start/session.send_input (reply blocks for the whole turn; terminal truth is the run.completed/failed/aborted event, which survives socket drops via replay), stream assistant.delta/reasoning.delta/tool.started|updated|finished/usage.updated/session.notice, answer approval.requested with approval.respond, run.abort, queue/steer follow-ups (delivery:"queue"|"steer" + session.pending_prompts), list/search/read history (session.list/search/messages), switch model mid-session (session.update_connection) and set per-session provider credentials (sessionConfig.apiKey/baseUrl/headers); stored credentials in ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json are merged server-side (prepareLocalRuntimeBootstrap.buildProviderConfig) so a key set once via `cline auth` in Termux works with no key in the app. Tools (bash/editor/readFile/search/webFetch/applyPatch) execute inside the Hub daemon in Termux when the client contributes no tool executors. MISSING vs the desktop sidecar (ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport, ~110 commands): no provider/model catalog (HubModelCatalog type is dead; `catalog.list` is not dispatched), no credential/provider CRUD or OAuth/ClinePass sign-in (settings.get/patch answer not_implemented; cline.account.get_current undispatched), no slash-command/@mention/file search (prompt_commands.*, mention_files.search undispatched), no workspace/dir picker, git/worktree/PR, MCP server CRUD (only settings.list/toggle), marketplace, voice; ask_question and checkpoints need the client to implement the capability.requested/respond contribution protocol; session.fork is declared but unhandled; after a daemon restart a conversation must be resumed by session.create with sessionConfig.sessionId (not verified end-to-end). Termux specifics: the daemon only starts with the port's entry.js + external `ws` fixes (a350d0d74, 54388558c); the app must get the Hub up (RUN_COMMAND `cline hub start`) and either read production.json via RUN_COMMAND or use Origin-header auth.
risks: Without toolPolicies {"*":{autoApprove:false}} (or per-tool entries) a Hub session auto-approves every tool, including bash and editor, because ToolPolicy.autoApprove defaults to true and the gate only fires on autoApprove===false; the CLI's own default is also autoApprove:true unless a persisted setting says otherwise.

An approval.requested with no client answering parks the turn indefinitely (no server-side timeout); it is only released by approval.respond, run.abort, an explicit per-turn timeout, or hub stop. The app must always resubscribe (approvals are re-issued) and offer abort.

The auth token changes on every daemon restart, so a token cached by the app goes stale; detect 401 on upgrade and re-read production.json (or rely on Origin-header auth, which also grants session creation in any workspace since session.create ignores connection authority).

Origin-header auth means any app on the phone that can open a loopback socket and set Origin: http://localhost can drive the Hub (create sessions, run bash via the agent) without the token — the token protects only /status,/drain,/shutdown and cross-workspace schedule/task scope. This is upstream behaviour, not port-specific.

run.start/session.send_input replies block for the whole turn with no server timeout; a client that sets a finite envelope timeoutMs gets hub_command_timeout while the turn keeps running. Terminal state must be taken from events, with sinceSequence replay after reconnects.

After the creating connection drops, createdByClientId is cleared; session.compaction.get/update then fail with session_wrong_client until a session.create/restore re-establishes a creator; capability-contributed features (ask_question, checkpoints) are cancelled on disconnect.

The server-side heartbeat terminates sockets that miss one 30 s ping cycle; Android Doze/background network throttling can therefore drop the socket roughly every minute while the app is backgrounded, after which the daemon unregisters the client and detaches it from sessions. Foreground service or reconnect-on-resume with cursor replay is required.

HUB_CAPABILITIES advertised in /health,/version and the discovery record do not match the real dispatcher (e.g. settings.set, session.run, session.abort advertised; settings.get/patch answer not_implemented) — do not drive feature detection from that list.

The Hub daemon on Android only exists because of the Termux port fixes (entry.js, external ws); upstream .68 never starts it, so any Android client depends on v3.0.68-termux.2 or later being installed.

Event-log replay stores every assistant.delta; a long reconnect gap replays the full backlog (pages of 200, up to 200k rows) — budget UI work and consider session-scoped subscriptions with recent cursors.
unknowns: Whether the `ws` server echoes the `cline-hub-auth.<token>` subprotocol in the 101 response (ws v8 default picks the first offered protocol when handleProtocols is unset, but the bundled ws version and bun-android-ffi behaviour were not checked); OkHttp rejects a handshake that offers a subprotocol the server does not echo. Test on device.

Resuming a persisted conversation after a daemon restart: session.create with sessionConfig.sessionId=<existing id> appears to resume artifacts (LocalRuntimeHost.startSession isReadOnlyResumeStart / resumedArtifacts, HubRuntimeHost plannedSessionId), but the full resume path (messages reloaded, usage restored) was not traced end to end.
Exact format expected for attachments.userImages strings (data URL vs base64 vs path) on the Hub side; userFiles are filesystem paths inside Termux.

Whether the daemon-side LocalRuntimeHost loads rules/skills/workflows from ~/.cline and the workspace itself when the client contributes no userInstructionService, and whether ask_question is simply absent from the tool list (vs. erroring) when no askQuestion executor is contributed.
Whether session.update_connection triggers any session.updated event (hub publishes none directly; runtime status/snapshot projection may).

The headless runtime tool names (BASE_TOOL_CATALOG headlessToolNames) that per-tool toolPolicies keys must use; only the catalog ids (read_files, search_codebase, run_commands, editor, fetch_web_content, web_search, skills, ask_question, tasks, spawn_agent, teams) were read.
Whether any CLI command prints the provider/model catalog as JSON for a RUN_COMMAND-based model picker (not searched).

Exhaustive confirmation that session.forked, artifact.created, diff.created, spoke.*, peer.* and hub.client.updated are never published anywhere (no publisher seen in the server handlers read; no repo-wide grep was run for those names).

readers.summary: Inventory of every user-facing Cline CLI/TUI feature at cli-v3.0.68 + Termux port (apps/cli/src), classified by entry point and by whether it is implemented in the CLI/TUI process (UI layer, filesystem/local) or by a kernel API an external client could call. Kernel API = the Hub WebSocket protocol (sdk/packages/shared/src/hub.ts, served by sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-server-transport.ts; CLI wrapper HubSessionClient in sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/session-client.ts) and, locally, ClineCore (sdk/packages/core/src/ClineCore.ts) which the TUI uses with backendMode "auto" (routes through the Hub when a compatible one is up, else in-process). Findings that matter for parity scoping: (1) the chat loop, session history, resume, checkpoint restore, pending-prompt queue/steer, abort, usage, team progress, schedules, agenda tasks, connectors and hub status are all reachable over the Hub protocol; (2) provider/model selection, API keys, OAuth/device-code sign-in, Cline account/credits, model catalog, settings-tab item lists (skills/rules/workflows/hooks/agents/plugins/MCP from disk), MCP/plugin/skill install, manual /compact's summarizer call, fork, history export, worktree, doctor, update, kanban, themes and input history are implemented inside the CLI process against Termux-private files or external tools, so an Android front end must bridge them through Termux RUN_COMMAND (`cline auth --provider --apikey --modelid`, `cline config <target> --json`, `cline history --json`, `cline hub status`, reading ~/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json for the authToken) or re-implement; (3) tool approval and ask_question over the Hub only work for the client that created the session and advertised the capability (`approval.respond`, `tool_executor.askQuestion`); (4) Hub auth is a WebSocket subprotocol `cline-hub-auth.<token>` or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; (5) the Termux port adds only touch-scroll/mouse env knobs, the Android default shell, and the Hub entry fix (a350d0d74, 54388558c on main, unreleased).
risks: Provider/model/API-key state lives in the ProviderSettingsManager file inside Termux's private dir and is read by the CLI process, not served by the Hub (no hub command exposes provider settings or the model catalog); an Android client must drive it through RUN_COMMAND (`cline auth --provider X --apikey K --modelid M`, `cline config --json`) and pass provider/model/apiKey explicitly in session.create / ChatStartSessionRequest as run-zen.ts does.

Tool approval, ask_question, submit, hooks, compaction, checkpoint creation, mistake-limit decisions and the user-instructions (skills/rules/workflows) snapshot are client contributions routed only to the client that created the hub session and advertised the capability (hub.ts: participants do not own capabilities). An app that attaches to a CLI-created session cannot approve tools; an app that creates sessions must implement these capability handlers or accept defaults.

Manual /compact is not a hub operation: the CLI runs its own summarizer LLM call (compaction.ts) and then calls session.compaction.update; an external client needs its own compaction implementation (or the compaction.compact capability).

session.fork is listed in HubCommandName but hub-server-transport.ts has no case for it; the TUI implements fork client-side (stop + start fresh with copied messages/metadata). Treat fork as not available over the wire until verified.

Hub auth token is only in ~/.cline/data/locks/hub/production.json (Termux-private); `cline hub status` deliberately omits it. The app must read it via RUN_COMMAND (needs allow-external-apps=true) and protect it; run.start/session.send_input hold the socket with no timeout, so Android background/doze handling matters.

The Hub daemon could not start on the device in any released Termux build (missing entry.js); the fixes are on main (a350d0d74, 54388558c) but unreleased, so all kernel-api items above are untested on the phone and depend on v3.0.68-termux.2 shipping.

History export (HTML), doctor, update, kanban, worktree, skill/plugin/MCP install and theming are process-local or external-tool features with no kernel API; parity requires RUN_COMMAND bridging or deliberate exclusion.
unknowns: Whether a hub session created by a client that does NOT advertise user_instructions.snapshot / compaction.compact / checkpoint.create still gets rules, skills, auto-compaction and checkpoints from the Hub process itself (handlers in sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-client-contributions.ts and runtime-host not traced to that depth).

Exact payload HubSessionClient.startRuntimeSession builds for session.create from a ChatStartSessionRequest (sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/session-client.ts lines 326-395 not read line by line); needed before writing an Android client.
The default production hub port value of CLINE_HUB_PORT (sdk/packages/shared) was not read; the task context states 25463.

The Cline Desktop sidecar protocol (ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport) and the cline-hub dashboard webview protocol were outside this lens; whether the Android app should reuse the dashboard web UI in a WebView (served by `cline dashboard --no-open`) was not evaluated.
The ACP agent's exact setSessionConfigOption keys and auth methods (ACP_AUTH_METHODS) were not enumerated.

readers.summary: Auth/provider/settings lens for the Android front end. Every credential and setting lives under ~/.cline/data (Termux-private): providers.json (API keys, OAuth tokens, lastUsedProvider, per-provider model), models.json (custom providers), global-settings.json (TUI/compaction/telemetry/tool toggles), cline_mcp_settings.json, and the Hub discovery record locks/hub/production.json (authToken). The CLI resolves provider/model/key at startup from flags > providers.json lastUsedProvider > "cline" (env CLINE_PROVIDER/CLINE_MODEL/CLINE_API_KEY are honoured only in ACP mode; provider-specific *_API_KEY env vars are a request-time fallback inside whichever process makes the model call, i.e. the Hub daemon). The Hub WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub, v1 envelopes, auth via Sec-WebSocket-Protocol "cline-hub-auth.<token>" or a loopback Origin header) exposes session.*, run.*, settings.list/settings.toggle (skills/workflows/rules/plugins/tools/mcp only), but settings.get/settings.patch reply not_implemented and there is no Hub command at all for provider catalogs, models, API keys, Cline account or global settings. A session uses a chosen provider/model by passing sessionConfig.providerId/modelId in session.create (omit apiKey entirely so the Hub merges the stored key / refreshes OAuth itself) or by session.update_connection on a live session; the Hub records provider/model in sessions.db and the per-session manifest. Cline Desktop gets provider/account/settings features from its own Bun sidecar (ws://127.0.0.1:3126/transport, commands list_provider_catalog, save_provider_settings, run_provider_oauth_login, cline_account, get_global_settings ...) which calls @cline/core in-process; the browser "cline-hub" dashboard (cline dashboard, port 8787) wraps the same functions over its own WS. An Android app therefore needs, for provider/key/account management, either Termux RUN_COMMAND wrappers around `cline auth ...` and file reads, or a resident helper process (the dashboard server or a custom one) in Termux; session history is readable over the Hub (session.list/session.messages/session.search) or from sessions.db + <sessions>/<id>/<id>.messages.json.
risks: Hub token-less loopback-Origin acceptance is an upstream convenience for browser clients; relying on it from the Android app may break when upstream tightens it, and it grants only daemon-workspace authority.
Reading or writing providers.json from a RUN_COMMAND script races the CLI/Hub (both rewrite the whole file atomically; last writer wins); prefer `cline auth` or core helpers over hand edits.

Hub auth token rotates on every daemon start; the app must re-read production.json (or /status) after `cline hub start|upgrade`, and the daemon's inherited env (proxies, *_API_KEY) is frozen at spawn time.
ProviderListItem/provider_catalog payloads carry plaintext API keys; any helper transport the app uses must stay loopback-only and avoid logging them.
The legacy secrets.json import silently re-creates deleted cline/openai-codex entries; sign-out must also clear those keys or the account comes back on next launch.

Desktop and CLI use different last-used sources (localStorage key cline.code.model-selection.v1 vs providers.json lastUsedProvider); an Android app that wants parity with the Termux TUI must track providers.json, which Hub session creation never updates.

session.create with apiKey:"" (not omitted) overrides a stored plain API key; endpoint-owned model catalogs (ollama, litellm, custom modelsSourceUrl) throw when the host is unreachable, so model lists need error handling.

cline-hub dashboard and the desktop sidecar are example/companion apps, not part of the Termux CLI package; shipping either on the phone needs its own packaging and its webview build is not verified in the Termux tarball.
unknowns: Default on-disk filename of the SessionHistorySearchService FTS database under ~/.cline/data/db (only the dbPath option was read).

Whether the Termux-packaged bundle resolves resolveClineBuildEnv() to "production" in every launch path so that production.json (not owners/<hash>.json) is always the discovery file (the task statement asserts production.json; not re-verified from the bundle).
How ClinePass visibility should be gated per account plan (feature flag ext-cline-pass is bypassed by current clients).

Whether `cline auth cline` (device-code flow) completes without a TTY under Termux RUN_COMMAND; the device path itself needs no prompt, but onPrompt uses readline if a provider asks for input, and the browser `open` call behaviour on Android was not checked.
Exact file name scope for the Hub event log/run queue on the device (derived: hub-events-hub-production.db / hub-runs-hub-production.db when ownerId is passed; not observed on disk).
Whether the hub's "browser-ws" transport kind or any other registration field changes command authorisation beyond the workspace checks read here.

readers.summary: Android integration constraints for a Compose front end to the Termux-hosted Cline kernel, with sources. Key findings: (1) Termux RUN_COMMAND is a usable control channel (action com.termux.RUN_COMMAND, dangerous permission com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND, allow-external-apps=true, results via a FLAG_MUTABLE PendingIntent, 100 KB truncation) and is the only way to read the Hub token file, since `cline hub status` does not print authToken. (2) The Hub binds 127.0.0.1:25463/hub, authenticates WebSocket upgrades with Sec-WebSocket-Protocol "cline-hub-auth.<token>", exposes an unauthenticated GET /health for liveness, and any app with INTERNET can reach it over loopback (local-network protection/ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK covers RFC1918/link-local ranges, not 127/8; cleartext to 127.0.0.1 needs a network-security-config entry below Android 17). (3) The Hub daemon dies with the Termux app process (AOSP kills the whole process group), so Termux must be kept in foreground-service state via termux-wake-lock (or an open session); Termux:Boot is only for reboot auto-start. The Android 12+ phantom-process killer (32 system-wide, excessive-CPU check only for procstate >= HOME) is disabled per device via adb device_config / settings / the Android 14+ Developer-options toggle; no app can do it. (4) The app's own WebSocket is cut ~10 s after backgrounding by the cached-apps freezer unless a foreground service runs; for targetSdk 34+ an FGS needs a type: specialUse (no timeout) or dataSync (6 h/24 h on Android 15+). (5) Toolchain as of 2026-10-03: AGP 9.4.0 + Gradle 9.6.0–9.8.0 + JDK 17 (built-in Kotlin, KGP >= 2.2.10; Kotlin 2.4.20 latest), compileSdk 37 (Android 17, API 37, released 2026-06-16; AGP 9.4 supports it), Compose BOM 2026.09.00 (ui 1.12.1, material3 1.4.0, adaptive-navigation 1.3.0), OkHttp 5.5.0; targetSdk 37 implies the large-screen adaptive enforcement with no opt-out (relevant on the Tab S7+).
risks: Hub lifetime: the Bun Hub is killed with the Termux process group (AOSP killProcessGroup) whenever TermuxService stops and Termux is later evicted; a RUN_COMMAND-started Hub without termux-wake-lock or an open session will silently disappear. The app must acquire/release the Termux wake lock itself and surface that state.

Phantom process limit is 32 across all apps and counts every cline tool subprocess; the excessive-CPU kill is skipped only while Termux's procstate is below HOME (foreground service). If the user clears Termux from recents or the wake lock lapses, long tool/LLM work can be killed as 'excessive cpu'. The only fixes are per-device adb/Developer-options changes the app cannot apply.

The token-less local-Origin WebSocket path (isLocalHubOrigin) means any app with INTERNET on the phone can open a reduced-capability Hub connection by spoofing an Origin header; do not rely on it for the app, and note it as a security consideration of the Termux deployment.

Choosing a dataSync foreground service imposes the 6 h/24 h budget on Android 15+ (targetSdk 35+) and a RemoteServiceException crash if onTimeout is not honored; specialUse avoids it but is a Play-review item if the app is ever published.
RUN_COMMAND results are truncated to 100 KB combined and the whole Intent to ~500 KB: fine for the token file, unsuitable for log tailing or transcript export.

targetSdk 37 removes the large-screen orientation/resizability opt-out; on the Tab S7+ (sw>=600dp) any portrait-locked or fixed-aspect screen will be ignored, so the UI must be adaptive from the start.
The cmdline-tools zip name and AGP/Gradle minimums move monthly; pin versions in the wrapper and version catalog and re-check the Studio download page when scaffolding.

Compose pre-release artifacts (1.13.0-alpha03, material3 1.5.0-alpha29) already require compileSdk 37.1 via the compileSdk { minorApiLevel } block; staying on the stable BOM 2026.09.00 avoids this for now.
unknowns: S25U device state could not be inspected (read-only rules forbid adb/ssh): its Android/One UI version, whether allow-external-apps=true is already set in ~/.termux/termux.properties, whether 'Disable child process restrictions' / settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs is already applied, and whether Termux is exempt from battery optimization.

Official Android docs do not say the word 'loopback' in the local-network-protection material; the conclusion that 127.0.0.1 is not gated rests on 127.0.0.0/8 being absent from the documented local-network ranges and on Android 17's implicit localhost cleartext config. Verify once with a targetSdk 37 build on an Android 17 device.
Grant behavior for the custom dangerous permission com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND when the app is installed before Termux (permission definer installed later) was not sourced; verify on device.

How to pin a Kotlin version newer than AGP 9.4's bundled KGP under built-in Kotlin, and how org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose interacts with built-in Kotlin, is not documented on the AGP 9.0 release notes or the migrate-to-built-in-kotlin page that were read; the AGP 9.4 notes also do not state the bundled KGP version.
The termux-wake-lock wiki page (wiki.termux.com) is behind an Anubis challenge and could not be fetched; wake-lock facts come from the TermuxService source instead.

Whether a background RUN_COMMAND (APP_SHELL runner) provides the full Termux login environment (PATH/LD_PRELOAD) needed by $PREFIX/bin/cline -> run-cline-termux.sh was not verified; Termux's AppShell sets up its own shell environment, but the port's launcher was not tested under it.
Whether the stable BOM 2026.09.00 artifacts compile against compileSdk 36 as well as 37 was not stated on the pages read; only the alpha train documents the 37.1 requirement.

Top-level views: chat (welcome state or conversation), sessions table, settings overlay with sections General | Providers | Voice | Channels(hidden) | Schedules | Import | Remote | Account | About plus Customize (installed hub) and Marketplace (explorer), onboarding overlay (welcome/connect/github/import/done), and a cloud-provisioning pane.
